description.before: Hyper-realistic companion android; 17 facial motors, swappable faces, wheeled base; bust from $10k
description.after: Aria is Realbotix’s established robot character and a historical named demonstrator, documented as a full-bodied greeter in 2025 and in an embedded conversational-AI demonstration in January 2026. The current Echo collection offers Aria as a persona on either Tabletop or Full Body hardware. This retained historical catalog identity does not specify a single current hardware configuration; unverified price, mass, travel speed, runtime and age limits have been removed.

description.before: Documented 2025 Realbotix B-Series platform. Manufacturer 2025 management report identifies an AI-enabled robotic bust. Report describes movement at 17 facial points and configurable language-model integration. Vision and body expansion are separately described options. Current new-unit availability and pricing are unverified.
description.after: The 2025 Realbotix report identifies B-Series as an AI-enabled robotic bust with movement at 17 facial points, third-party language-model integration and optional vision/full-body expansion. The IFA announcement describes a vision-equipped demonstration configuration. Seventeen facial points are not an established mechanical DOF count; current new-unit pricing, stock and first launch remain unverified.

dof.after: 39 degrees of freedom in the 2025 manufacturer report

terrain.after: Stationary from the waist down; upper-body movement

description.before: Documented 2025 Realbotix M-Series platform. Manufacturer 2025 report identifies a modular robot with a stationary lower body. 39 degrees of freedom support coordinated upper-body movement. Manufacturer describes portable packing for demonstrations and events. Current new-unit availability and pricing are unverified.
description.after: The historical Realbotix M-Series is a modular full-bodied platform stationary from the waist down, with 39 manufacturer-stated degrees of freedom for upper-body/facial expression. Manufacturer documentation describes suitcase-sized transport and a vision-equipped IFA demonstration. Later Echo Full Body specifications are not transferred; exact current offer, mass, dimensions, electrical endurance and initial release remain unknown.

batteryLife.after: 4–8 hours estimated in the 2025 report; load and usage conditions unspecified

dof.after: 44 degrees of freedom in the 2025 manufacturer report

terrain.after: Motorized wheeled base; surface and grade limits not published

description.before: Documented 2025 Realbotix F-Series platform. Manufacturer 2025 report identifies a full-bodied platform on a motorized wheeled base. 44 degrees of freedom support expressive body and facial movement. Integrated battery and mains operation are documented for this older platform. Current new-unit availability and pricing are unverified.
description.after: The 2025 Realbotix report describes F-Series as the highest-tier full-bodied historical robot with a motorized wheel base, integrated battery and 44 manufacturer-stated degrees of freedom. Mains operation or an estimated 4–8 hour battery duration is described without load/test conditions. This is not a verified 480-minute maximum; exact current sales configuration, travel speed, mass and first launch remain unknown.

description.before: Compact tabletop platform provides expressive head and facial movement. Announced October 26, 2026 with initial delivery planned for the second half of 2027. Operation requires a monthly app subscription; optional Vinci vision is a separate upgrade.
description.after: Echo Tabletop is one of two Echo hardware platforms announced on October 26, 2026, with 17 stated degrees of freedom and approximately 25 lb mass. Manufacturer dimensions distinguish footprint from female/male height. Planned delivery starts in the second half of 2027; reservations are currently limited to US addresses. A separately paid monthly AI plan is required, Vinci vision is optional, and Aria/Mila/Dave/Amar are persona choices rather than additional hardware models.

notAdditionalCards: Aria/Mila/Dave/Amar persona choices on two Echo platforms; no eight extra hardware cards.
David CES and Melody event names do not establish separate standard hardware SKUs.
Vinci vision, AI plan tiers, digital twins, facial/body customization and integration services are options/software/customization, not additional powered robot models.
unresolvedMappings: Exact historical Aria demonstrator configuration not established; old physical and fixed-price claims removed.
B/M/F first launch, current supplied configurations, pricing/stock, mass, dimensions and IP unknown.

validation.initialValidationFindings: Application/unit/build/audit and both browser selections passed on the first run. The copied scratch rendered-export checker initially expected 54 fields from the prior 18-field arm schema; corrected to 51 for three 17-field humanoid reviews, then passed. This was a checker count correction; no application or data change followed validation. Product matrix and persona table were parsed by named columns and asserted separately.
validation.scope: Fourteen source attempts, thirteen HTTP 200 bodies including two PDFs / 28 text pages. One FAQ DNS failure excluded. Thirty-four selected browser cases including eight axe runs, not the full browser suite. Manufacturer figures are not independent testing; Echo is pre-production and delivery remains a future estimate.
